headline: Rhode Island directs $5.48M to rural school healthcare career pathways
dek: Fourteen districts and schools will use Rural Health Transformation funds for healthcare training, from middle-school exploration to hands-on high school programs.
body: Rhode Island is directing more than $5.48 million in federal Rural Health Transformation Program awards to 14 school districts and schools, creating or expanding healthcare career pathways in rural communities across the state.

The Rhode Island Department of Education announced the awards Wednesday at Ponaganset High School in Glocester. The department said the grants are designed to connect students with health careers in stages: career awareness in kindergarten through fifth grade, exploration in grades six through eight, and preparation for work or further study in grades nine through twelve. The announcement was also reported independently by [Providence Business News](https://pbn.com/foster-glocester-lands-largest-share-of-5-48m-rural-healthcare-cte-grants/).

The money comes through the federal Rural Health Transformation Program, which is supported by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. Rhode Island says the broader program is intended to improve access to coordinated healthcare in rural communities. RIDE said its awards will reach the state’s 18 rural communities, while helping schools build relationships with healthcare providers and colleges.

Foster-Glocester Regional School District received the largest award, $1,360,343. The district plans to anchor its pathway at Ponaganset with an on-campus physical therapy clinic, physical and occupational therapy programs, and a middle-school wellness initiative that introduces younger students to health careers. That design gives students a local setting to encounter the field before they have to choose a high school concentration or postsecondary program.

Other awards target distinct parts of the healthcare pipeline. Burrillville Schools received $928,574 for a biomedical sciences pathway and a new EMS and health sciences learning center, with possible training in emergency medical services, nursing, phlebotomy, physical therapy and related fields. East Greenwich Public Schools received $710,619 to launch what RIDE described as Rhode Island’s first pre-medicine career and technical education program, while modernizing learning spaces and adding work-based learning, medical simulation and AI-supported clinical tools.

Westerly Public Schools received $658,773 to improve its medical careers and EMS pathway with simulation equipment, virtual-reality training, staffing and professional development. Smithfield received $513,690 to expand biomedical sciences and add behavioral-health training. Scituate received $318,191 to extend its biomedical pathway through the K-12 grades and add sports medicine, community health and emergency-response options. The remaining grants range from $25,604 for Jamestown’s Lawn School to $268,454 for Narragansett High School, with projects also planned in Chariho, Exeter-West Greenwich, Little Compton, North Kingstown, North Smithfield and at The Greene School.

The awards are arriving as Rhode Island expands its overall career-and-technical-education system. RIDE reported that the number of high-quality CTE programs statewide has grown from 203 in 2019 to 365, while participation has increased from about 12,000 students to more than 20,000. Those figures are the department’s comparison, not an independent evaluation of the new grants, and the announcement does not provide a single completion date for the 14 projects.

The next phase will be local implementation: districts will have to turn the awards into courses, equipment, work-based learning and partnerships that students can actually use. For rural Rhode Island, the practical test will be whether the new pathways make healthcare careers visible earlier, provide meaningful clinical or technical experience, and create durable connections between schools, employers and the communities that need healthcare workers.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Rhode Island awards $5.48M for rural healthcare training
seoDescription: Fourteen Rhode Island schools and districts received more than $5.48 million to build rural healthcare career and technical education pathways.
